bugs.description: Bot asked for service despite customer having 'typical_services: [Corte de Mujer]' in seeded memory (customer_memories). The agent_notes explicitly state 'Siempre pide Corte de Mujer'. R-41 (grounded preferences) requires resolving 'lo de siempre' from DB history rather than asking.

Bot did not use seeded memory (preferred_stylist_name='Marta', typical_services=['Corte de Mujer'], visit_count=8) to proactively resolve 'lo de siempre'. The customer's clear reference to their usual service was ignored.

turns.user_message: Lo de siempre... el corte de mujer de siempre. Siempre pido lo mismo.
turns.agent_response: ¿Para quién es el corte: señora, caballero, niña, niño o bebé?

bugs.description: Bot asked audience disambiguation despite: (1) customer is a returning female customer (Raquel Cordero), (2) seeded typical_services=['Corte de Mujer'] already specifies a female service, (3) customer explicitly stated 'corte de mujer'. The bot is ignoring existing customer context.

turns.user_message: Para mí, señora. Corte de mujer, como siempre.

bugs.description: Bot correctly flagged Carmen as not in catalog but did NOT proactively surface 'Marta' as the customer's preferred stylist from memory (preferred_stylist_name='Marta'). It listed all stylists generically instead of guiding the customer toward their known preference: 'No tenemos Carmen, pero tu estilista habitual es Marta, ¿te va bien?'

¿La aceptas?

bugs.description: Bot triggered policy gate for a returning customer who had already accepted policy v1.0 (policy_accepted_at seeded ~300 days ago, policy_version='1.0' matching POLICY_VERSION default). The <customer> block from CustomerResolveMiddleware should contain 'Política privacidad: aceptada v1.0 el ...' but the bot is re-requesting acceptance. This is a regression of R-41 grounded-preferences / policy gate not being respected for returning customers.

turns.agent_response: Perfecto. ¿Me dices tu nombre y primer apellido?

bugs.description: Bot asked for name/surname despite the customer existing in DB with first_name='Raquel', last_name='Cordero'. The <customer> block includes 'Nombre: Raquel Cordero' — the bot should use this known name rather than re-asking a returning customer for their identity.

Bot asked 'qué servicio quieres reservar?' despite seeded memory having typical_services=['Corte de Mujer'] and agent_notes stating the usual service. R-41 violation: 'lo de siempre' must resolve from DB history, not be re-asked.
Bot did not leverage any of the seeded customer_memories (preferred_stylist_name, typical_services, visit_count=8) to proactively resolve 'lo de siempre'. This is the core R-41 failure.
Bot asked audience disambiguation (señora/caballero/niña/niño/bebé) after customer said 'corte de mujer de siempre'. Context from memory and user statement was sufficient.
When Carmen was not found, bot listed all stylists generically instead of surfacing Marta as the known preferred_stylist_name from memory.

Bot triggered policy acceptance gate for a returning customer who already accepted policy v1.0 (policy_accepted_at set, policy_version='1.0' = current POLICY_VERSION). Policy re-gate is incorrect — CustomerResolveMiddleware should inject the accepted status and the booking flow should skip the gate.
Bot asked for customer name/surname despite customer existing in DB as 'Raquel Cordero'. The <customer> block contains this information.

seed_notes: Customer seeded with: 3 past completed appointments (Corte de Mujer with Marta), customer_memories.typical_services=['Corte de Mujer'], preferred_stylist_name='Marta', visit_count=8. No stylist named 'Carmen' exists in DB (persona references Carmen — bot correctly reported Carmen not in catalog at turn 4).
